page.layout: One column of dictionary entries (Hebrew headwords with Latin glosses), running from top to bottom. The page number is at top right, the running head at top centre, and a catchword at bottom right. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: ראשית f. Principium; Primum, Præstantissimum; Primitivum, Primitiæ: ראשי דנגך Primitiæ frumenti tui, Deut.18.4. ראשית דע Principium scientiæ, Proverb.1.7. Semel absque Aleph, מרשית A principio anni, Deuter. 11.12. Aff. מראשיתו Præ quàm principium ejus; Eccles.7.9.
ראשות f.p. Primordia: Aff. מראשתיכם Præ primordiis vestris, Ezech.36.11.
ראשות f.p. Cervicalia, quasi Capitalia dicas: Constr. cum terminatione masculina; מראשתי שאול A cervicalibus Saulis, 1.Sam.26.12.
מראשות f.p. Idem: Aff. מראשתו Versus cervical ejus, 1.Sam.26.7.
מראשות f.p. Principatus: מראשתיכם Principatus vestri, Jer.13.18. id est, Quælibet & omnis dignitas vestra.

רבב Multum, Copiosum esse, Multiplicari: Jacular, à Vicino Verbo רבה: Præterit. ורבקים Et fulgura jaculatus est, Psal.18.15. juxta Ab.Efram, & Kimchium in Commen. Nam priori significatione semper intransitivum est. Et sic juxta eosdem, ורבו Et jaculati sunt, Gen.49.23. רבו Multiplicant, Psalm.4.8. Fœmin: כי רבה Quia multa est, Gen.18.20. Infin: לרב Multiplicari, Genef.6.1. Pyh.Particip. מרבבות Myriadibus auctæ sint, myriades pariant; Psalm.144.13. quæ significatio à Nomine רבבה petita est.

רב m. Multus, Magnus, Major; Amplus: Magister, qui multis præfectus est, aut multos doctrinâ & dignitate antecellit. Quandoque subst. Multum, Magnum, & Adverbialiter, Multùm, Satis: רב עם Populus multus, Josh.11.4. ישלי רב Est mihi multum, frater mi, Gen.33. v.9. רב לכם Satis esto vobis, Numer.16.3. עם כל רב ביתו Super unumquemque magistrum domus sua, Esther.1.v.8. מושיע

page.notes: Several Hebrew words are uncertain at this scan resolution, notably ראשי דנגך (probably ראשית דגנך), ראשית דע (probably ראשית דעת), מרשית (probably מראשית), ורבקים and the catchword מושיע. These are marked [?] where they stand or flagged here. The Latin glosses and references are read as printed. The Hebrew in the first entry is copied as seen, not from a standard text. Italic is applied to the Latin glosses and to the headwords as they appear in the scan. The watermark at bottom right is not transcribed.
